resources.string:
Apps you put in the Secure Folder run in a hidden profile with its own lock and its own encryption key. It isn\'t shown in the app drawer, as a tab or as a section.
Next you\'ll choose its passphrase and, if you like, keyfiles.
Nothing here yet. Use ⋮ → Add apps.
Secure Folder icon in the app drawer
4 to 16 digits. Dial *#*#code#*#* to open the folder. The code is stored only as a salted hash.
Everything in the folder is gone for good: its apps, files and its encryption key, which is erased from the phone\'s secure hardware. Type DELETE to go on.
The app you shared from didn\'t give access to the file, so it can\'t be moved.
Unlock the Secure Folder, then share again.
There\'s no Secure Folder on this phone.
A Private Space already exists. Delete it in Settings first; its lock can\'t take a passphrase with keyfiles.

12 to 256 characters: a few unrelated words is easier to type and harder to guess than a short mix of symbols. Add keyfiles if you want: every one is needed each time, in any order.\n\nIf you forget the passphrase or lose a keyfile, nobody can open the folder again, not even with the phone\'s own lock.
A keyfile couldn\'t be read and wasn\'t added.
Setting the lock… (a few seconds, on purpose)
This folder wasn\'t made by Secure Folder, so it can\'t be opened here.
Too many tries. Wait a while, then try again.
This Android doesn\'t let Secure Folder open the folder with its own lock screen. Secure Folder needs AnonpheneOS.
The lock is changed. The old passphrase and keyfiles no longer work.
After %1$d wrong tries in a row
